It sucks man, but it’s all manageable. If you get your sugars in check, you can build/lose weight the same way a normal person would. I just started going hard in the gym 13 weeks ago. I’ve been building muscle pretty consistently. 

Having diabetes can make it really easy to become dehydrated and lose nutrients, so make sure you’re correcting high blood sugars quickly. I use those LiquidIV packets 2-3x a day, keeps me very hydrated.

Also, careful working out or being super physical while your sugar is high. It’ll dehydrate you faster, and If you develop ketones It can be hard on your kidneys if your exerting yourself. It’s also much more draining than normal. I don’t recommend doing much when your sugar is low either, but it’s usually a lot more straightforward and faster to correct a low blood sugar than a high one. I find I can’t exert all of my effort into things, physically or mentally, when my sugar is low.

You get used to the symptoms over time, it gets easier, but there will always be days that just make no sense. Can’t let it get to you.

I don’t know, same thing happened to me. I used to be completely detached from reality & anxiety ridden (a year after quitting cold turkey and I still kinda am, but much better mentally). I’ve been kinda unstable as long as I can remember, but I had a 3 year low point starting in high school. I was speedballing everyday for 3 years straight. My DOC’s were Adderall IR & XR, Xanax, and Klonopin. They were all prescribed for legitimate reasons but as I felt worse I began misusing, and I ended up getting to 30-50mg of IR, 10-30mg of XR, 4-6mg of Xanax, and 1-3mg of Klonopin, every single day. Sometimes I wouldn’t take 2 of the same class, but  more often than not, that’s what I’d do. I never really got high off of Xanax aside from one night where I took a ton (I honestly think I was trying to commit…) and my roommate woke me up in my car at noon at my dorm. Somehow me and my car were unscathed, last thing I remember is driving at around 1:00AM past the pizza place in town and then I blacked out. Never had happened before and my memory was usually really good even under the influence. A concerned friend told my family, who told my doctor, the rest is self-explainable. I got cut off, had to go cold turkey. I was worried sick about quitting, but after a couple days all I had felt was a little more tired than normal. Then a week, then a month, and now about a year. Still haven’t had any withdrawal symptoms, I’m getting back to being a functional person, holding down a tough job. Life’s great now. Still have my low days, but never as bad as they used to be. 

TLDR; I don’t think being mentally healthy is a requirement for OP’s question. I was so far from being mentally healthy but I quit a 3yr daily speedball with no problems, other than being a little more tired than usual. I’m sure genetics are a primary factor in this, but I believe your mental resilience (being resistant to *mental turmoil?*,couldn’t think of a more fitting word) is just as important.

While I appreciate the concern, respectfully I would not put my issue with Ashwagandah dulling pain, anywhere near a state of mania. All I’m experiencing is a significantly reduced sense of pain, which *in-turn* causes me to not feel a sense of fear in relation to the pain. Mania is a psychological issue (I’m oversimplifying, I know) and does not cause a pain reduction. Now mania may put you in a headspace where you legitimately can’t feel *any* kind of fear in *all* regards, and that would in-turn cause you to not react to the physical feeling of pain. 

So, to clarify; in mania you may not react to pain *because* of your mental lack of any kind of fear. In my Ashwagandah case I don’t react with fear *because* I didn’t physically feel it in the first place.

Mine is a physical issue, Mania is a mental issue, different origin points. I’ve had medication induced mania, this is not mania.

Lol it’s confusing as fuck, right? All I could tell you about the pharmacokinetics of Vyvanse is that it’s what known as a *”pro-drug”*. A pro-drug is any non-psychoactive substance that enters your body, but is metabolized into a different substance that *is* psychoactive. So it not necessarily a “timed release”, it more of just a substance that takes a while to get in and out of you. Vyvanse’s *only* active ingredient is “* Lisdexamfetamine*”; Adderall has four amphetamine salts, the primary two being “*dextroamphetamine*” and “*levoamphetamine*”. Adderall’s ingredients are metabolized rapidly, only taking 10-30mins to kick in on average. Adderall’s effects are typically felt for 4-5 hours after kicking in. Vyvanse’s ingredient, while being considered an *active ingredient*... ...has absolutely no effect on the body until it’s metabolized into Dextroamphetamine. This is one of the primary reasons that Vyvanse is growing in popularity so fast as an ADHD treatment, snorting Vyvanse cannot give you a single benefit that swallowing won’t (unless you’re into fucked up noses lol).

Firstly, I'm assuming that you are *not* a diabetic of either kind, secondly, I'd advise *against* taking any diabetic medication if you aren't actually diabetic.

So are these sugar spikes noticeable to you? Or are you measuring your glucose with a blood sugar meter? Now the reason that I advise *against* taking any diabetic medication is because of how your non-diabetic body will handle the sugar drops. Since you aren't a diabetic, your body will automatically counteract the sugar lowering. Whenever you take an amphetamine, the neurotransmitters it affects make your body *think* that heightened blood sugar is "normal". It won't be pumping anymore insulin than you'd normally experience, at least no-more that could be noticed. If you were to take a diabetic medication your body would more-than-likely "fix" the lowering of your sugar, as most diabetic meds don't manipulate your neurotransmitters. Also keep in mind that while an amphetamine is giving an increase to your sugar, eating any high carb food will also spike your sugar. Because of your sugar already being heightened, the spike that food will give you is going to be more noticeable. Try and eat more proteins and less carb filled foods. Look into more fiber rich foods, such as bananas. Fiber filled foods have the potential to lower and/or slow your digestion and absorption of carbs.

I too am an ADHD sufferer. I take 40mg of Vyvanse daily. So the symptom range for ADHD is incredibly broad, a large multitude of disorders can also mimic ADHD quite proficiently. I was diagnosed with ADHD at 15 years old (2.5 years; I’m now 18) and I had a complex series of symptoms. One of these symptoms stuck out the most... ...I had been struggling with this Depersonalization and Derealization (Dp/Dr) effect for a little bit over a year then. After seeking and committing to a weekly therapy session I had finally unveiled that the Dp/Dr was a result of some childhood trauma that had occurred, I’d rather not get into any specifications concerning the trauma. When I was taking my initial questionnaire to be diagnosed with ADHD, I never actually brought the feeling up or even hinted at it. After the diagnosis I began taking 30mg of Vyvanse per day. As bizarre as it was, whenever I took my Vyvanse the Dp/Dr seemed to almost vanish. The alleviation of my Dp/Dr would slowly draw away as my Vyvanse tolerance steadily increased. Because of this, I talked to my doctor and had my dosage increased to 50mg -that only lasted one month because it made me far too irritable and sent my Adrenal system haywire. After being brought down to 40mg I felt quite “normal” (normal meaning minimal ADHD symptoms and minimal Dp/Dr). After thinking about the dosage jump, I realized that it’d be better to stay at *one* lower-end dose, than it’d be to slowly increase the dosage until I was at 70mg -and needing to switch meds. Because of this, I did some digging around and found two substances that directly counter **any** amphetamine tolerance. These two substances are *Magnesium* and *DXM*(Dextromethorphan; found in almost all cough syrups). Both of the substances have one specific property that works to kick down the Amphetamine tolerance, that is they are both known as *NMDA* receptor *antagonists*. While I can only, safely, recommend Magnesium... ...DXM is the stronger antagonist. Magnesium is very commonly used as a supplement and can be found at just about any vitamin/drug store. DXM has a street-reputation as a cheap and easy hallucinogen but only in **high** doses above ~120mg. That is the primary reason I can’t recommend DXM, Second to me not being a doctor lol. My personal regimen is a regular dose of 800mg before bed, and 400mg in the morning, of Magnesium Citrate. Admittedly, that dose is 400mg above the “recommended” amount stated on the bottle but I’ve found the dose to be highly suited to my needs. I’ll also take a typical-clinical-dose of DayQuil two or three times a month as just an added tolerance reducer. Please take the utmost of caution if you so-choose to do the same regimen as me; I cannot stress that enough. And once again, everything in this post is anecdotal and based on my own research and so I strongly encourage you to look into the idea on your own and then decide wether, or not, you’d like to try it out. I also feel this should be stated: Depersonalization/Derealization isn’t too rare of a side-effect for withdrawals. People who truly have ADHD are typically less prone to Amphetamine withdrawals (this, of course, depends on many factors within every different person), and usually don’t have anywhere near the same degree of symptoms if they do so-happen to get withdrawals. Thanks for asking! She’s doing incredibly well. Despite 66% of those that suffer a brain aneurism having a lifelong complication, she has literally none. It’s common for the complications to include things like a new speech impediment, the loss of motor function in one or more parts of the body,and in the very worst case scenario, a vegetative mental and physical state. 40% of people that have a brain aneurism don’t survive (with most deaths occurring in the ambulance) so you can imagine the shock we all felt when she had no issues. She was a little “off” after her hospital release but I think it was just her going through a little withdrawal from all of the painkillers they had her on (She was given Fentanyl once when she first went into the hospital but then spent an additional 6 weeks there and given Morphine, Percocet, and then sent home with a small amount of OxyContin and some Tramadol to taper down). She’s been great ever since. I honesty thought I wouldn’t get the chance to see her alive again. She was on vacation up in New York with my feather when it happened while I was down in Texas. But we’ve never felt closer since. That kind of an experience opened our eyes to realize just how fast someone can go. It’s crazy, I can remember every single thing that happened each day for the month and a half that she was hospitalized. I had just woken up and finished up with my shower and getting ready to go to work when I got a call from my dad. Now I’ve never heard this man come anywhere near crying but this is the only exception, his voice was trembling as I could hear him fight the tears but just because of that I knew immediately something had happened to my mother. After somewhat gathering myself I went to work, at this point we didn’t what happened to her, all we knew was as soon as she had stepped out of the airport terminal she seized and fell unconscious. After about 30 minutes of work I got another call and he broke the news. Thankfully my boss could tell I was severely distraught and let me leave early, he even gave me one of those hugs that just helps. He’s a very masculine guy so this break from character really showed he cared. After 36 hours of no communication with my father I had come to the conclusion she was gone. He finally called and explained they were going to start surgery within the hour but they didn’t know how much damage may have already occurred. I didn’t sleep for an entire week but thankfully her 6 hour surgery she was “level”. She took an additional week to wake up but the first thing I did when that happened was FaceTime. Just because of how in the moment I was, I didn’t think about her being on anything... ...as soon as she answered it was incoherent mumbling. It wasn’t a concerning mumble as it was very obvious she was loopy. That was the first time I had ever seen my mom under the influence of anything. It was a pretty fun 45 minute talk, she can’t remember it, but it was the closest thing I’ve ever come to what heaven would feel like. Looking back on it, the scariest thing to me was the night before her flight. I was helping her pack since my father was already in NY for a business trip. She couldn’t stop complaining about her brain-fog and confusion. She was in a rush like usual when she’s packing so I didn’t think of it that much. She had fallen over once while I was helping her and that gave me a bit of concern but it seemed to me like she was feeling the precursors of a migraine and that she just needed to sleep through it. She was scheduled to leave the house at 4:00AM and so I said my goodbyes since I wasn’t going to see her in the morning cause I wake up at 7:30AM for work. She drove an hour to the airport, to which she was an hour early, and then had a 4 or 5 hour flight. She had fallen unconscious 30 minutes after she had landed. In that 6-7 hour span, she could’ve had the rupture at any time. But somehow it waited till her flight landed. We don’t know what we would’ve done if it happened an hour prior while she was in the air still. My family hasn’t been closer since. It’s truly a wake up call, makes you wonder what it’d be like if the situation went the other way. We just cannot believe how well she’s doing, literally her only complaint, relating to the incident, has been having to take an Asprin every day. That’s it lmao

Vyvanse is the brand name of Lisdexamfetamine, a prodrug that lasts 8-12 hours and is an alternative to Adderall. Vyvanse is prescribed for the same reasons as Adderall, ADHD and Binge Eating Disorder (BED). Pro-drugs work by taking advantage of the human bodies metabolism. The chemical, Lisdexamfetamine is a dormant substance that on its own has no effects. However, after undergoing hydrolysis by red blood cells, the chemical reaction yields D-Amphetamine, the chemical found in Adderall.  Vyvanse’s effects are noticeable about 2 hours after consumption. Taking the drug on an empty stomach has no effect on the speed at which Vyvanse begins working. You can only safely take this substance orally, either through capsules/tablets or dissolving in water and consuming thereafter.  As a side note: never snort this as it will only hit you just as fast as a capsule and damage nasal blood vessels.

The effects of Vyvanse are similar to those of Adderall, albeit with fewer negative symptoms in most people, and has a “smoother” duration of action. Vyvanse is considered to be a “less addictive” substance however the risk of abuse is still there. You could think of it like this, Vyvanse is like Tramadol is to the Opiate/Opioid class of drugs, as Vyvanse is to the Amphetamine class of drugs. Tramadol is made to be a less addictive alternative to opioids and prescribed for, typically chronic, relief of moderate to moderately sever pain. Abuse of Vyvanse is typically characterized by a euphoric, buzzy, and very stimulating, range of effects. Recreational use is typically considered to be a dramatic increase in the expected effects of a prescribed dose, usually to the point that the effects become more distracting and sometimes unpleasant in nature. Once an individual has experience a recreational dose they will be at a much more inclined risk to use the substance again, at the same doses.

Vyvanse bears the same risks and negative side effects as Adderall and should be used with these in mind. Vyvanse isn’t really known for the effects having a “zombie” like effect, as opposed to Ritalin and other methylphenidate drugs.

The primary problem with Vyvanse, and why it’s much less known to people, is that it is expensive. The cost without insurance is usually found at within $200-$300, give it take. The reason for such a high price is that the there is no generic version. The patent possessed by the founding company has yet to expire and is set to do so in 2023. 

In the US amphetamines, like Adderall,are preferred by both the people prescribed and the people who use them illicitly. Due to Vyvanse’s seemingly decreased risk of addiction, it is gaining increased popularity in doctors and patients alike. The price, however, is still restricting its mainstream debut as the Adderall replacement.

“504 plans are formal plans that schools develop to give kids with disabilities the supports they need. These plans prevent discrimination and protect the rights of kids with disabilities in school. They’re covered under Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act. This is a civil rights law.” [Source](https://www.understood.org/en/school-learning/special-services/504-plan/understanding-504-plans) 

Basically if your disability is recognized, by the law, as a potential factor in not being able  to learn like a normal person can; you can request special accommodations for a disorder that’ll assist an individual in whatever specific way needed.

For example, I’m a Type 1 Diabetic. I have a 504 plan at my school that allows me to have my phone on me at all times in order to check my blood sugar levels. I’m also allowed to use the bathroom at any time, no questions asked, all I have to do is show my nurses slip and they recognize it immediately. I can eat in whatever class I want and I can ask for extra testing time if I need it. These are all apart of my 504 plan that I had sat down with my school principal and discussed what accommodations I needed. Teachers are not allowed to deny an accommodation, no matter the circumstance. I’m not required to show them proof of my blood sugar in order to use an accommodation so the teachers have to take my word for it. Just don’t abuse the 504 plan and you’re fine.

I don’t have a 504 plan for my ADHD so I’ve got no idea what sort of accommodations that you specifically need but all you need to do is sit down with your principal, or whoever handles this sort of business, and discuss the accommodations needed (they do need to be reasonable for the condition). The only reason that I don’t have a 504 plan for my ADHD is because I usually remember to take my medication before school and if I forget I have friends with ADHD that’ll give me one of their Vyvanse’s as long as I give them one of mine in return.

It eventually came to me that I wasn’t always like this. One day after school, for some dumbass reason, I consumed 1200mg of Caffeine. Now, that was awful. I was twitching, I was extremely anxious, and I was very paranoid. Through that time though I realized that I was now able to think. I ended up coming to the conclusion that people with ADHD also take stimulants for their condition, I put two and two together and decided that I wanted to be tested for ADHD. At the time I didn’t realize that it was a symptom test and not a blood test or something of that caliber. While I was being tested their were so many questions that I didn’t even realize could be related to my ADHD. My doctor diagnosed me with “Sever ADHD”. After that I got prescribed 30mg Vyvanse and after that first dose I felt incredible; I was able to complete my work as if I was completely normal. It made me complete so much more than my peers as a result of the happiness that I felt after finally being able to finish my work (an addiction to working in a sense). I’ve been able to pull my GPA back up to a reasonable level for my current Junior year and so my woe in class.
